Hendo on AWS — Technical Evaluation FAQ

Follow-up to an AWS agent-platform technical deep dive, 22 July 2026. Answers reflect the AWS services as they run today; forward-looking and beta items are marked as such.

This FAQ is scoped to running agent workloads inside the customer's own AWS account and VPC. The default and commercial model is a self-hosted deployment that integrates directly into Amazon Bedrock, Bedrock AgentCore, and Amazon SageMaker. No customer data leaves the VPC.1

1 · Deployment & consumption model

How is an agent platform deployed — container, AgentCore runtime, or a Bedrock agent?

Container is the default — the whole platform is containerized and deploys into the customer's VPC. For the agent runtime specifically, you have two current options: run agents in your own container, or run them on the Bedrock AgentCore runtime (serverless, session-isolated on Firecracker microVMs)2. The choice is the customer's — the platform supports both.

One naming point, since it matters to an AWS SA: this is the current AgentCore path, not the legacy Bedrock Agents (Classic) product, which is closing to new customers on 30 July 2026. New deployments target AgentCore.

Is the platform a SaaS offering, or do we deploy it in our own AWS VPC?

For commercial use, you deploy it in your own AWS VPC — that is the default and the only commercial focus. Roughly 99% of customers run self-hosted inside their own account. A hosted tier exists only for education and startups on free credits; it is not the enterprise path.

2 · Architecture & orchestration

What is the orchestrator? Is it LangGraph?

The primary orchestrator is a first-party orchestration layer alongside a manager-style pattern for agent-of-agents coordination. It is built on an open-source agent framework, not on LangGraph. LangGraph is not required and is not the engine; if a team already has LangGraph graphs, they can be imported and run inside the platform, but the orchestration the platform provides is first-party.

Does the customer own the agentic orchestration layer, or does the vendor?

The customer owns their agents, knowledge bases, and workflows outright. The foundations are open: the core runtime is open source and the agent framework is a first-party framework built on an open protocol.[Customer references pending clearance for written use — see editorial notes.]

3 · Data & governance

Is there a data governance and ingestion layer for agents?

Yes. Ingestion pipelines are built on the orchestrator, and knowledge bases support live sync with sources like SharePoint. On the AWS-native side, work is under way on Iceberg on AWS for open, governed table storage feeding agents.

Does the platform integrate with the agent-management / governance systems we already run?

Yes. It supports identity porting from systems like SharePoint and carries those existing policies across into the platform, so agent access respects the governance you already have rather than creating a parallel silo.

4 · Observability & monitoring

Does it integrate with AWS monitoring — specifically CloudWatch?

Yes, through open standards and the AgentCore runtime:

  • OpenTelemetry into CloudWatch, natively. The platform emits telemetry over OpenTelemetry (OTLP). Amazon CloudWatch ingests OTLP directly — traces and logs through its OTLP endpoints,3 and OTEL metrics reached general availability in mid-20264 — so telemetry lands in CloudWatch without a bridging collector.
  • Native by default on AgentCore. When agents run on the Bedrock AgentCore runtime, AgentCore Observability routes distributed traces, span-level logs, and metrics to CloudWatch by default under the bedrock-agentcore namespace.5

5 · Compute footprint

What's the compute footprint when deployed in our VPC?

The platform runs entirely in the customer VPC across a defined set of managed AWS services. The core data and state layer includes:

LayerAWS service
Document / metadata storeAmazon DocumentDB
Relational storeAmazon Aurora PostgreSQL
Search / vectorAmazon OpenSearch
Object storageAmazon S3
CacheAmazon ElastiCache

Model and agent compute (Bedrock, AgentCore runtime, SageMaker) sits on top.
